gaps: No pipeline-stage caching / non-destructive re-processing feature. The chain (clip -> extracted frames -> keyed -> cleaned -> quantized) must keep every intermediate on disk and re-run only downstream stages when the user changes a TOL slider or palette size. Without this, every knob tweak re-extracts or (worse) re-generates, and the raw frames needed to re-key are gone after a destructive pass. sprite-project-persistence stores settings but never states that originals are retained and stages are re-runnable/invalidated.

No cancellation feature anywhere. core/video/veo_client.py and omni_client.py have no cancel/abort hooks (verified by grep), and no catalog feature covers cancelling an in-flight per-action queue, a whole-clip ffmpeg key preview, or a per-frame rembg batch (seconds-to-15s per frame on CPU). A 7-action Veo batch the user cannot stop is both a UX failure and a cost failure.

No threading/progress contract for the tab. The repo's Video GUI uses QThread workers per dialog; the catalog never assigns keying, quantization, ffmpeg extraction, de-jitter, or ML matting to worker threads with progress + responsive UI. For a PySide6 tab this is a core architectural feature, not an implementation detail — several listed operations are multi-second-to-multi-minute.

No undo/redo. frame-strip-manager allows reorder/delete/duplicate/duration edits and ai-frame-retouch overwrites frames in place, with no undo model anywhere. Every surveyed editor (Aseprite, Piskel) has undo; destructive frame deletion without it will lose user work.

No keyboard-shortcut spec. The repo has a hard dialog convention (Ctrl+Enter primary, Escape close) and sprite editors have de-facto standards (Space play/pause, comma/period frame-step, onion-skin toggle). No feature claims them; retrofitting shortcuts after layout ships is painful.

No error-handling/safety-filter feature for generation failures. Veo/Gemini refuse humanoid characters, minors, and IP-lookalike characters (person_generation policy, RAI filters) — the single most likely first-run failure for a game-character workflow — and nothing defines the user-facing message, the logged error (house rule: every user-facing error is logged), retry/backoff on 429/quota, or a route fallback when one model refuses. The gpt-image-2 caps gating is covered; policy rejection is not.

No 'exact-N frames' selection stage. Every-N extraction plus manual culling yields a variable frame count, but the sprite spec is 'an 8-frame walk cycle'. A feature that picks the best N temporally-uniform frames (or resamples to exactly N) is the missing bridge between clip-timing-hints' math and the sheet the engine expects.

No automated frame-quality QA. The loop-seam meter grades loops, but nothing auto-flags morphed/off-model frames (per-frame diff vs neighbors or vs the character reference) so the user knows WHICH of 120 extracted frames to retouch or cull. Manual eyeballing across 7 actions x 15+ frames is the dominant time cost of the whole pipeline.

No import of an existing video clip or PNG sequence into the processing spine. The maintainer said chroma is 'for after images are generated ... apply chroma to the frames' — that implies keying arbitrary frames, including clips made in the Video tab or elsewhere. send-to-sprite only routes still images; sheet-import-slicing only handles grids. A 'process this video/frame-folder' entry point makes the whole Frame Processing category usable standalone and is cheap.

Palette lock + remap on regeneration is unspecified. shared-palette-quantization builds the palette from the union of all frames, but the catalog's own risk list expects per-action re-renders; nothing says the palette is then locked and new frames are remapped to it (Aseprite 'Remap'), or that the palette is versioned in the project. Without lock semantics, one re-rendered action re-flows every action's colors.

Source-resolution sufficiency check missing. A 16:9 720p Veo clip leaves the character perhaps 250-400px tall; after union-bbox crop that supports a 64px cell but not the 96/128px presets. No feature validates 'character pixels available vs target cell' and warns or routes through the upscaler before downscale.

Cost estimator has no stated price source and no post-hoc spend ledger. Rates change; the estimator should pull from a maintained table (the repo already vendors a model registry) and the project should record actual per-action spend so users learn real iteration cost. Also nothing surfaces VeoClient's max_concurrent/quota limits in the queue UI.

Disk-usage management absent. Clips + extracted frames + intermediates for a multi-character project are gigabytes; no cleanup/'purge intermediates' feature, and the new sprite_projects() accessor must also be added to the PR #42 storage-migration journal or moving the storage root will orphan sprite projects.

Per-frame processing overrides unspecified. Key color, TOL, and matte model are global per action; AI clips routinely have one frame where the key fails. Without per-frame override (or the later MobileSAM escape hatch promoted), one bad frame forces re-render.

Dependency claims are overstated: mediapipe is NOT a shipped dependency — it is runtime-installed via core/character_animator/installer.py (requirements.txt only pins protobuf 'for mediapipe compatibility'), so ml-background-removal's 'zero-install path' actually inherits an install-on-demand flow that needs UI. numpy arrives only transitively via opencv; scikit-image/scipy (frame-dejitter) are wholly new deps needing the 7-day-age check. opencv-python is confirmed present.

Testing strategy uncovered: no feature/phase gate names golden-file tests for exporters (Aseprite JSON vs paladin.json, .tres, GIF-trap regression, palette-file byte layouts) or headless-safe smoke tests for the SpriteTab per the repo's dialog-smoke-test convention; only the risks section hints at it.

HD (non-pixel-art) sprite path is implicit but not first-class: binary-alpha-128 and quantization defaults assume pixel art, yet the maintainer never said pixel art — modern engines happily consume soft-alpha 256px+ sprites. A 'skip pixel-art conversion' toggle with soft-alpha exports must be an explicit supported path, not the absence of Phase 3.

Frame-rate metadata in exports vs maintainer's 'number of frames per second': defaults store per-frame ms, good — but no feature writes fps/timing into the plain grid-PNG + filename-only export path (the no-metadata fallback), e.g. a sidecar txt/json or filename token, so grid-only consumers lose timing entirely.
open_questions: Phase-1 route conflict: the catalog makes the Veo/Omni video route the Phase-1 flagship, but your request leans image-first ('Nano Banana Edit ... might even produce several frames', 'GPT Image 2 can produce animations too'). Which route ships in Phase 1 — video, image, or both? This decides most of Phase 1's cost and scope.

Is pixel-art conversion (quantization, binary alpha, integer downscale) the default output path, or an optional branch beside an HD soft-alpha sprite path? Your request named palettes/colors but not pixel art explicitly; defaults like binary-alpha-128 hinge on the answer.
Sprite CLI is scheduled Phase 2, but the house rules treat CLI parity as expected for headless pipelines. Accept the deferral, or pull a minimal CLI (process+export, no generation) into Phase 1?
What Python versions must ImageAI keep supporting? rembg pins >=3.11,<3.14 and the answer gates whether it can even be an optional extra.

New hard dependencies to approve for Phase 1/2: scikit-image + scipy (de-jitter) vs an OpenCV phaseCorrelate-only fallback; and is promoting mediapipe from runtime-installed to a declared optional extra acceptable?
Undo model: full command-stack undo for frame edits, or the cheaper 'non-destructive + snapshot on destructive ops' model? Affects the frame-strip and retouch designs from day one.

Content policy: is the tab allowed to send user photos of real people (or trademarked characters) to Veo/Gemini at all, or should it pre-warn/block? Determines the error-handling design and support burden.
Cost controls: should the batch queue require an explicit confirmation above a spend threshold (e.g. >$1 estimated), and should per-project actual spend be recorded in the SpriteProject?
Default cell size 64x64 and default video length 8s at 720p — confirm, or prefer 4s veo-3.1-fast drafts as the default to cut iteration cost?

Where should intermediates live and how long: keep raw clips + extracted frames forever in the project (re-processable, large) or offer auto-purge after export? Also confirm sprite_projects() gets added to the storage-migration journal.
